    World Trade Organization (WTO)

     WHAT

        WTO was formed in 1995 with the signing of Marrakesh Agreement by 123
            countries in Morocco.

          The Marrakesh Agreement was signed on April 15, 1994 at the conclusion of the
          Uruguay Trade Rounds.

          Main activities of WTO –

                Negotiating the reduction or elimination of obstacles to trade (import tariffs,
               other barriers to trade) and agreeing on rules governing the conduct of
                 international trade (e.g. antidumping, subsidies, product standards, etc.)

               Administering and monitoring the implementation of the WTO's agreed rules for
                trade in goods, trade in services, and trade-related intellectual property rights.

               monitoring and reviewing the trade policies of the member countries, as well as
               ensuring transparency of regional and bilateral trade agreements.





International Organisations                                                                                                           3

settling disputes among the members regarding the interpretation and
                 application of the agreements

                building capacity of developing country government officials in international
                trade matters.

     WTO Trade Principles:

           Trade without discrimination -

               Most-favoured-nation (MFN): treating your trading partners equally

                National treatment: Treating foreigners and locals equally

            Freer trade: gradually, through negotiation

             Predictability: through binding and transparency

               Countries provided their rate of custom duty and committed not to increase it
             beyond the commitment

           Promoting fair competition

           Encouraging development and economic reform



     WHY

        History of WTO

              In the Bretton Woods Conference of 1944, which is also known as the United
           Nations Monetary and Financial Conference, all the 44 participating countries
           agreed to establish three organizations to control the world economy.

          The organizations were –

                International Monetary Fund (IMF)

                International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), also known as
                the World Bank

                International Trade Organization

          The major reason behind establishing all these organizations was to avoid the
             repetition of the Great Depression of 1930s.

          IMF and IBRD came out as a success but ITO could not achieve the success in its
            implementation.

          By 1947, countries became desperate to establish an organization for regulating
            trade after the end of World War II.

           Thus, on October 30, 1947, a total of 23 nations agreed to sign an agreement called
           “General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade” (GATT) for regulating trade, until ITO is
            formally established.





International Organisations                                                                                                           4

In 1948, Havana Charter was adopted in Havana, Cuba to give a shape to ITO.

             56 countries, except USA, signed the charter to establish ITO.

                  In 1950, US announced its withdrawal from ITO.

           Without US, which was a major economy at that time and even today, the Charter
          and the ITO itself became ineffective.

           Thus, GATT continued to govern the international trade till 1995, when it was
            abolished and World Trade Organization was formed.

       WTO is not a specialised agency of United Nations, like IMF and World Bank.



       Drawbacks of GATT and the Need for WTO:-

       Trade Rounds of GATT:

             Eight trade rounds were organized during the GATT years from 1948 to 1994.

          1. Geneva (1947),

          2. Annecy (1949),

          3. Torquay (1950-51),





International Organisations                                                                                                           5

4. Geneva (1956),

          5. Geneva (1960-61) - also known as the Dillon Round,

          6. Kennedy Round (1964-67),

          7. Tokyo Round (1973-79),

          8. Uruguay Round (1986-94) – in this round, the consensus for establishing WTO was
             arrived at.

        Organizational Structure of WTO:





          The Ministerial Conference is the top most decision making body of WTO, which
           comprise of ministers of member countries.

                    It brings together all members of the WTO, all of which are countries or customs
            unions.

          The Ministerial Conference can take decisions on all matters under any of the
              multilateral trade agreements.

              Ministerial Conference meeting is conducted once in every two years.



       Governance of WTO

          The member countries frame the rules of trade at the Ministerial Conferences.

          The Director-General of WTO is also appointed at the conference.





International Organisations                                                                                                           6

The main responsibility of the Director-General is to oversee the functioning of the
              staff of WTO Secretariat in Geneva. Thus, the duties of the D-G is managerial in
             nature. The D-G has no policy-making power.



        Dispute Settlement Mechanism of WTO

          The major achievement of WTO is its dispute settlement mechanism which was
            missing in the erstwhile GATT.





       TRIPS Agreement

           TRIPS stands for Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights

                    It protects the Intellectual Property Rights in the global trade.

           TRIPS came into being, along with WTO, in 1995.

              In 2001 WTO Ministerial Meeting in Doha, Qatar, Doha Declaration on the TRIPS
          Agreement and Public Health clarified that “the TRIPS Agreement can and should be
             interpreted and implemented in a manner supportive of WTO members' right to
            protect public health and, in particular, to promote access to medicines for all”.

             The Doha Trade Round was expected to conclude in 2005.

                Since, the members are not able to reach a consensus on many pertinent issues,
                 therefore, the conclusion of this trade round has been postponed indefinitely or
                             till the time a resolution is attained.



      Need for Reforms in the WTO





International Organisations                                                                                                           7

There are certain issues in the WTO that hamper its effectiveness.

          The most contentious issue in the WTO is the unresolved trade round that is pending
            since 2005.

         Many issues have emerged in the present international trade with new emerging
            technologies and growing animosity between the countries.

               For e.g., US-China trade war (during the Former President Donald Trump’s reign)
            was started because US retaliated against China’s intellectual property theft
                   unilaterally, without waiting for the WTO’s resolution report, by imposing tariffs
             on China. This triggered a tariff war between US and China.

           US even criticised WTO for admitting China as a member.

               This tariff war impacted business worldwide. Although the impact was not of a
                great scale. Still, this trade war defeated the very purpose of WTO’s existence.

           Another major reason for the increasing inefficacy of WTO is the languishing
            Appellate Body.

                 Till now, there are no members in the Appellate body of WTO, which is a crucial
           organ of the Dispute Settlement Mechanism of WTO.

    United Nations (UN)

     WHAT

      UN was established to promote international cooperation. It replaced the ineffective
       League of Nations after World War II in order to prevent another such conflict.

         Potential members in UN are recommended by the Security Council and are admitted
       by a two-thirds majority vote in the general assembly.



     WHY

          The United Nations was born of perceived necessity, as a means of better
              arbitrating international conflict and negotiating peace than was provided for by the
            old League of Nations.

          The growing Second World War became the real impetus for the United States,
              Britain, and the Soviet Union to begin formulating the original U.N. Declaration,
           signed by 26 nations in January 1942.

          The principles of the U.N. Charter were first formulated at the San Francisco
           Conference, which convened on April 25, 1945.

       TELL ME MORE

        UN has 6 principal organs-





International Organisations                                                                                                           8

1. The General Assembly - the main deliberative assembly under which all members
          and secretary general meet to address standing issues.

          2. The Security Council - establishment of peacekeeping operations, the
            establishment of international sanctions, and the authorization of military action
           through Security Council resolutions. There are 5 permanent members in security
            council namely China, France, UK, US and Russia. 10 other countries have
           temporary membership on a Rotation basis.

          3. The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) - for promoting international economic
          and social co-operation and development.

          4. The Secretariat - It is the executive arm of UN. It implements decisions taken by
           above- mentioned bodies. Secretary general is the head of secretariat.

          5. The International Court of Justice - Seated in the Peace Palace in The Hague,
            Netherlands, the court settles legal disputes submitted to it by states and provides
            advisory opinions on legal questions submitted to it by duly authorized international
           branches, agencies, and the UN General Assembly. Decisions of Cases taken to ICJ
           are not always binding.

              There are two types of cases- contentious issues and advisory opinions.

                  In contentious cases adversarial proceedings seeking to settle a dispute), the
               ICJ produces a binding ruling between states that agree to submit to the ruling of
                the court.

               Advisory opinions are only consultative in character

          6. The United Nations Trusteeship Council (inactive since 1994).



       League of Nations

                    It was established in 1920 in Geneva, after the signing of a treaty at the Paris Peace
           Conference of 1919.

             After 26 years of its establishment, the League of Nations gets abolished in 1946
          because of its failure in preventing the World War II.

                    It had 43 member countries at the time of its abolition.

    World Bank

     WHAT

       The World Bank is a United Nations International Financial Institution that provides loans
         to developing countries for capital programs.

                    It was created in 1944 after the Bretton Woods conference.





International Organisations                                                                                                           9

IMF and WB are called Bretton Woods Twins

         Two ambitious goals

             To push extreme poverty to no more 3 percent by 2030

             To boost shared prosperity of the poorest 40% of the population in all countries

     WHY

          The 1944 Bretton Woods Conference established the World Bank. Its loans helped
           European countries rebuild after World War II. That made it the world's first
              multilateral development bank.

                    It was funded through the sale of World Bonds.

                Its first loans were to France and other European countries.

              In the 1970s, it lent money to Chile, Mexico, and India to build power plants and
             railways. By 1975, its loans had helped with a wide variety of issues. They included
             family planning, pollution control, and environmental protections.

       TELL ME MORE

       World Bank Group comprises of 5 organizations-

          1. International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)- established in
            1944, it generates money through debt financing and provides developmental
            finance to member countries.

          2. International Development Association (IDA)established in 1960, it provides
            concessional financing (interest-free loans or grants), usually with sovereign
            guarantees. Together, IBRD and IDA make up the World Bank.

          3. International Finance Corporation (IFC)established in 1956, it provides various
           forms of financing without sovereign guarantees, primarily to the private sector of
            the developing countries.

          4. Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) established in 1988, it provides
            insurance against certain types of risk, including political risk, primarily to the private
             sector. It also provides credit enhancement guarantees.

          5. International Centre for settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) Established in
           1966, works with the government to reduce investment risks. It is world’s leading
              institution devoted to international investment dispute settlement.



        Reports Published By World Bank

           World Bank Group is a part of United Nations System. The World Bank's (IBRD and
            IDA) activities are focused on developing countries, in fields such as human
           development (e.g. education, health), agriculture and rural development,
            environmental protection, infrastructure etc.





International Organisations                                                                                                          10

IBRD and IDA provide loans at preferential rates to member countries, as well as
            grants to the poorest countries.

             India is a member of 4 institutions under world bank group. It is not a member of

    The International Bank for Reconstruction and
    Development (IBRD)

     WHAT

       IBRD is world’s largest development bank. It provides financial products and policy
        advice to help countries reduce poverty and extend the benefits of sustainable growth
         to all of their people.

                    It supports the World Bank Group’s mission by providing loans, guarantees, risk
          management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy
           low-income countries, as well as by coordinating responses to regional and global
            challenges.



     WHY

          The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and International
           Monetary Fund (IMF) were established by delegates at the Bretton Woods
           Conference in 1944 and became operational in 1946.

          The IBRD was established with the original mission of financing the reconstruction
              efforts of war-torn European nations following World War II.

            Following the reconstruction of Europe, the Bank's mandate has transitioned to
            eradicating poverty around the world.



       TELL ME MORE





International Organisations                                                                                                          11

IBRD joins with IDA to work closely with all institutions of the World Bank Group and
            the public and private sectors in developing countries to reduce poverty and build
           shared prosperity.

    The International Development Association
     (IDA)

     WHAT

       The International Development Association (IDA) is the part of the World Bank that helps
        the world’s poorest countries.

        IDA aims to reduce poverty by providing loans (called “credits”) and grants for programs
         that boost economic growth, reduce inequalities, and improve people’s living conditions.



     WHY

           IDA is one of the largest sources of assistance for the world’s 75 poorest countries,
         39 of which are in Africa, and is the single largest source of donor funds for basic
             social services in these countries.



       TELL ME MORE

           IDA lends money on concessional terms.

            This means that IDA credits have a zero or very low interest charge and repayments
            are stretched over 30 to 38 years, including a 5 to 10-year grace period.

           IDA also provides grants to countries at risk of Debt Distress (Distressed debt refers
             to the securities of a government or company which has either defaulted, is under
           bankruptcy protection, or is under distress and moving towards the aforementioned
             situations in the near future).

    The International Financial Corporation (IFC)

     WHAT

              It is the largest global development institution focused exclusively on the private sector
          in developing countries. It helps developing countries achieve sustainable growth by
         financing investment, mobilizing capital in international financial markets, and providing
        advisory services to businesses and governments.



     WHY

           IFC was founded on a bold idea that the private sector is essential to development.





International Organisations                                                                                                          12

TELL ME MORE

           IFC raises virtually all funds for lending activities through the issuance of debt
             obligations in international capital markets.

          The borrowings are diversified by country, currency, source, and maturity in order to
            provide flexibility and cost effectiveness.

           IFC is the only multilateral source of debt and equity financing for the private sector
            with global reach

    The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency
    (MIGA)

     WHAT

      MIGA provides political risk insurance and credit enhancement for cross borders private
        sector investors and lenders.

                    It aims to promote foreign direct investment into developing countries to support
          economic growth, reduce poverty and improve people’s lives.

                    It does this by providing political risk insurance (guarantees) against certain non-
          commercial risks to cross-border investments, as well as by providing dispute
            resolution services for guaranteed investments.



     WHY

         MIGA was established as an effort to complement existing sources of non-
           commercial risk insurance for investments in developing countries



       TELL ME MORE

       Miga can help investors and lenders deal with these risks by insuring eligible projects
         against losses relating to:

          Currency Invertibility and Transfer Restriction - Protection against losses arising
           from an inability to legally convert local currency into hard currency

            Expropriation - Protection against losses arising from certain government actions
             that may reduce ownership of the insured investment

           War, Terrorism and Civil Disturbance - Protection against loss from, damage to, or
           disappearance of tangible assets caused by political acts of war or civil disturbance.

          Breach of Contract - Protection against losses arising from government’s breach or
            repudiation of a contract.





International Organisations                                                                                                          13

Non-Honouring of Financial Obligations – provides coverage for credit
          enhancement in transactions involving sovereign and sub-sovereign entities, as well
           as state-owned enterprises. Protects the lender against losses resulting from a
              failure to make a payment when due under an unconditional financial payment
             obligation or guarantee.

    The International Centre for Settlement of
    Investment Disputes (ICSID)

     WHAT

       The ICSID has been established to provide facilities for conciliation and arbitration of
         international investment disputes. It was established for legal dispute resolution and
         conciliation between International Investors.



     WHY

            Several attempts were made to create a framework to protect international
            investments, but efforts revealed conflicting views on how to provide compensation
              for the expropriation of foreign direct investment.

           Thus, in 1961, then-General Counsel of the International Bank for Reconstruction and
           Development (IBRD), Aron Broches developed the idea for a multilateral agreement
          on a process for resolving individual investment disputes on a case by case basis as
          opposed to imposing outcomes based on standards.



       TELL ME MORE

              It is an autonomous, multilateral specialized institution to encourage international flow of
        investment and mitigate non-commercial risks by a treaty drafted by the International
       Bank for Reconstruction and Development's executive directors and signed by member
         countries.

     International Monetary fund (IMF)

     WHAT

          IMF was established along with World Bank to bring economic stability in the
             international market.

          The main objectives of IMF comprise of: -

                Fostering global monetary cooperation

              Secure financial stability





International Organisations                                                                                                          14

Facilitate international trade

              Promote employment

              Promote sustainable economic growth

             Reduce poverty

          IMFs financial year is from May 1 to April 30.



     WHY

        History of IMF

          The IMF was conceived at a UN conference in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire,
            United States, in July 1944.

            At the Conference, all the 44 members (present at the conference) realised the need
              for an international organization to stabilize the volatile world economy.

          The countries wanted to build a framework for economic cooperation to avoid a
             repetition of the Great Depression of the 1930s.

              In light of the volatility in the economic, social, and political front in the post- war
            world, the countries decided to establish a mechanism to regulate foreign exchange
             rates, manage money international market, and global economic situations.

          The IMF has played a major part in shaping the global economy since the end of
           World War II.



        Functions of IMF

            Providing Financial Assistance – It provides financial assistance to its member
            countries via short-term loans. Its assistance aim to correct the economic imbalance
              in the country.

                 Further, to correct the economic situation in the countries, IMF provides
               consultancy to the countries which are facing Balance Of Payments (BOP)
                   difficulties.

                 Also, IMF helps governments of members countries to ensure responsible public
               spending.

                         It also provides consultancy to countries for modernizing their economic policies
             and institutions.

            Surveillance – IMF monitors the global economic situation, international monetary
           systems, and economic policies of countries.

             IMF is also responsible for keeping exchange rates in check to facilitate inter-
                transactions between countries.





International Organisations                                                                                                          15

Therefore, it regularly monitors policies, innovations, emerging trends, etc. that
             can impact international markets.

           Capacity Development – IMF also aims to provide technical assistance and training
             to central banks, finance ministries, tax authorities, and other economic institutions.

             IMF also helps countries in achieving their SDGs.



       TELL ME MORE

      Where does IMF get its funding from?





       Funding Source: Subscription by Member Countries: -

          IMF allocates Quota to its every member, in return for its membership.

         Member countries have to pay their contribution (equivalent to Quota) as: -

           25% must be paid in SDRs or foreign currencies acceptable to the IMF (such as
                the US dollar, the euro, the Chinese renminbi, the Japanese yen, or the British
             pound sterling)

                   This 25% contribution is known as the ‘Reserve Tranche’ of the country.

                    Contributing country is free to use this 25% contribution, without drawing
                 any interest or penalty from the IMF.





International Organisations                                                                                                          16

But, if the withdrawal of the country exceeds the Reserve Tranche, then, IMF
                     levies penalty on that country.

           75% is paid in the member's own currency

        Benefits of Quota:





International Organisations                                                                                                          17

What are Special Drawing Rights (SDR)?

         SDR was created in 1969 by IMF, 24 years after its formation.

          The main purpose of SDR is to support the foreign reserves of countries.

           Before 1969, countries used to keep their foreign reserves in gold and US Dollars,
           which led to an unprecedented hike in the prices of these assets.

              In order to keep the prices of gold and USD in check and maintain economic
               stability, IMF created Special Drawing Rights (SDR).

         SDRs are used as a component of foreign reserve assets of many countries
             (including India).

          Even the countries’ contribution to IMF is denoted in the form of SDR. On these
           SDRs, IMF pays interest to the countries.



         Points to be noted:

         SDR is not a currency because currencies are created by countries and IMF is not a
            country.

               Secondly, SDR does not have its own inherent value. Instead, its value is
              determined by a basket of currencies.

                    It is not a claim on IMF.

             Rather, it is a reserve asset that can be exchanged among countries for foreign
            currencies.





International Organisations                                                                                                          18
International Organisations                                                                                                          19

The value of one SDR is determined by a basket of 5 currencies namely:

           US dollar- highest weightage

              Euro

             Yen

                  British pound

              Chinese Renminbi (joined the basket in 2016, thus, it is the latest)

          The SDR value in terms of the U.S. dollar is determined daily.

             Interest on SDR – It is calculated on a weighted average of representative interest
             rates on short-term government debt instruments in the money markets of the SDR
           basket currencies, with a floor of 5 basis points.



       Governance of IMF

          IMF is controlled and managed by a Board of Governors.

          Each member country nominates its own governor and all nominated governors
         make the board of governors.

          Each governor is allotted a number of votes, which is determined by the quota
              allotted to the respective country in IMF.

           Thus, voting rights are determined by quota. This is the reason why the rich and
             industrialized countries have a higher voting right due to higher quotas with the IMF.



        Reports Published by IMF

           World Economic Outlook

            Regional Economic Report

            Global Financial Stability Report

     International Labour Organization (ILO)

     WHAT

          The International Labour Organization (ILO) is a United Nations agency dealing with
            labour problems, particularly international labour standards, social protection, and
          work opportunities for all.



     WHY





International Organisations                                                                                                          20

The ILO was founded in 1919, in the wake of a destructive war, to pursue a vision based
       on the premise that universal, lasting peace can be established only if it is based on
         social justice.

          The ILO became the first specialized agency of the UN in 1946.



       TELL ME MORE

       The main aims of the ILO are to promote rights at work, encourage decent employment
         opportunities, enhance social protection and strengthen dialogue on work-related
         issues. ILO serves the society as a whole in the following ways-

            Formulation of international policies and programmes to promote basic human
              rights, improve working and living conditions, and enhance employment
            opportunities

            Creation of international labour standards backed by a unique system to supervise
              their application

         An extensive programme of international technical cooperation formulated and
           implemented in an active partnership with constituents, to help countries put these
             policies into practice in an effective manner

             Training, education and research activities to help advance all of these efforts

    United Nations Educational, Scientific and

            the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

            orderly growth.

          and facilitation of border-crossing procedures for international civil aviation.

          ICAO defines the protocols for air accident investigation followed by transport safety
             authorities in countries signatory to the Chicago Convention on International Civil
            Aviation.

International Maritime Organization (IMO)

     WHAT

         IMO has the responsibility for the safety and security of shipping and the prevention
            of marine and atmospheric pollution by ships. Its main role is to create a regulatory
           framework for the shipping industry that is fair and effective, universally adopted
          and universally implemented.



     WHY

           Inter-Governmental Maritime Consultative Organization (IMCO) was formed in
            order to bring the regulation of the safety of shipping into an international
           framework, for which the creation of the United Nations provided an opportunity.

                    It was later renamed the IMO in 1982 and has continued to produce new and
           updated conventions across a wide range of maritime issues covering not only
            safety of life and marine pollution but also encompassing safe navigation, search
          and rescue, wreck removal, tonnage measurement, liability and compensation, ship
             recycling, the training and certification of seafarers, and piracy.



       TELL ME MORE

                Its role is to create a level playing-field so that ship operators cannot address their
              financial issues by simply cutting corners and compromising on safety, security and
            environmental performance. This approach also encourages innovation and
             efficiency.

          The Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) is an integrated
           communications system using satellite and terrestrial radiocommunications to
           ensure that no matter where a ship is in distress, aid can be dispatched.

          Under the GMDSS, all passenger ships and all cargo ships over 300 gross tonnage
          on international voyages have to carry specified satellite and radiocommunications
           equipment, for sending and receiving distress alerts and maritime safety information,
          and for general communications.

          The GMDSS became fully effective from 1 February 1999. It is currently undergoing
           a comprehensive review.
